searches.note: Twenty eight searches of a share of twenty eight, none of them the author's. Fourteen were restricted to a house's own domain (tascadalmerita.it four times, donnafugata.it three times, benanti.it twice, the two De Bartoli domains three times, cosvittoria.it three times) and are read as primary through their summaries; two went to the Etna and Cerasuolo di Vittoria rules. Two searches gave nothing (a Benanti search in Italian with no wine words, an Italian search for the De Bartoli case on open domains) and were followed by narrower ones. One further call naming a domain the search tool refuses was rejected before it ran and is not counted. No WebFetch was tried. Every record was tested; no fact that rests on no source was kept.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year, the people and their dates, the classification and its year, the grapes, the sites, the making and its months, the drinking window, the serving temperature, the label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules (nobody living named, no price, no score, nothing volatile, no judging superlative, no bare family word, British spelling, no dash).

The searches went first to the dates and people (each founding, Giacomo Rallo, Giuseppe Benanti, Marco De Bartoli, the case of 1995), then to the rules (Etna Bianco Superiore, Cerasuolo di Vittoria and its Classico), then to the sites and the making the author had from the houses' sheets, then to the story beats the author had on one account.

Where a search contradicted the record it was set right with its source; where a detail the author gave could not be found again and no second search found it either, it was cut (the training of San Lucio and of the COS vineyard, the drying time of Ben Ryé, the Khamma opening of 2006, the old casks of COS).
Sources whose title or address names a living person were read in the results but never cited in the fragment; the fragment's own sources were left as the author wrote them.

tested: Founded 1830: the purchase of Regaleali by the brothers Lucio and Carmelo Mastrogiovanni Tasca, about 1,200 hectares, the house's history page and sustainability reports: confirmed; the brothers stay described for want of their dates.
The land reform: the postwar agrarian reform cut the estate from about 1,200 to 500 hectares (the house's pages): confirmed, more than half kept.

San Lucio planted in 1959 by the count, Perricone and Nero d'Avola mixed, about 5.5 hectares, with about 1.5 hectares of Nero d'Avola alone in 1965 (the house's narrative; the 2019 sheet gives 1965 alone as the planting year, the Riserva sheet 1959): confirmed and made exact in sites.

The 1970 vintage sold as Riserva del Conte, later called Rosso del Conte, and the house's claim of the first single vineyard wine of Sicily (the house's pages): confirmed, the claim told as the house's.
The appellation: Contea di Sclafani DOC on the house's pages and most merchants; Falstaff and two merchants list some vintages as Sicilia DOC: kept, left open.
The blend: 58 and 42 per cent (2017, 2018), 62 and 38 (2019), 53 and 47 (2018 elsewhere), 63 per cent with other estate reds (2012), 54, 26 and 20 (2016): changed.
The site: 480 metres on every sheet; south south east on most documents, south west on one; loamy sand, partly calcareous: aspect changed, the rest confirmed.
The making: about twenty days on the skins in steel, about eighteen months in 225 litre French barriques of Allier and Tronçais (the Italian 2019 sheet and the merchants): confirmed.

Riserva del Conte: back in production in 2010 after forty years, from the same vineyard, aged in 500 litre chestnut barrels in homage to its origins, 26 months in new chestnut by the 2016 sheet; the blend is Perricone 60 per cent on one house page and Vinous, Nero d'Avola 60 per cent on the house's shop page: changed.
Lucio Tasca's Cabernet Sauvignon and Chardonnay at Regaleali (the house's pages): confirmed as the count's son planting international varieties.
The house rules: nobody living named; no price, score or superlative; British; no dash: sound.

changed.why: No sheet or merchant read gave equal shares: Nero d'Avola runs 53 to 62 per cent in 2017 to 2019, and the 2012 and 2016 took in other estate reds. Recent was refused by the lint as volatile, so the vintages are named by decade.

tested: Founded 1983 by Giacomo Rallo and his wife, the name from The Leopard chosen by her, the Marsala cellars of 1851 (the house's roots and company pages, Wein.plus, the house's profile): confirmed.
Giacomo Rallo born in Marsala in 1937, died in 2016 (the house's own pages): confirmed; the dates now rest on the house beside Decanter.
Contessa Entellina: the house says she took ownership and leadership of the family estate there a few years before 1983; no source read said she inherited it from her father: changed.

The queen of the legend: Maria Carolina fleeing Naples before the French and finding refuge where the vineyards lie, as the house tells it (the house's roots page, Wein.plus; the year is the early 1800s in one account and 1798 in another): confirmed as the house's account, the queen kept unnamed.
Arrival on Pantelleria in 1989 and the first Ben Ryé of 1989 (the house's timeline and its 2023 sheet): confirmed.
The Khamma winery opened to visitors in 2006: not found; the house's page and FAI give the walled garden at Khamma restored and given to FAI in 2008: changed.

The making: the first picking in the first half of August (2023) or from 17 August (2019), the dried grapes stripped from their stalks by hand and added in batches to the fresh must as it ferments in temperature controlled steel, over a month in all; four, five and seven months in tank and ten, sixteen and twelve months in bottle on the 2022, 2023 and 2016 sheets; no sheet read gave three to four weeks of drying: changed.
UNESCO's inscription of 2014: the house's own page on the alberello vine as UNESCO heritage beside the author's UNESCO page: confirmed.
The house rules: the wife and children unnamed; no price, score or superlative; British; no dash: sound.

changed.now: founded Donnafugata, with the family's vineyards at Contessa Entellina, which she had taken in hand a few years before.
changed.why: The house says she took ownership and leadership of the family estate a few years earlier; how she came to it is not in any source read.

tested: Founded 1988 at Castiglione di Sicilia on the northern slope as Tenuta di Castiglione, the grandfather's winemaking at Viagrande, two experimental harvests, the first bottled vintage 1990 (the house's timeline and 2020 profile, Wine Spectator, which adds that the house took the family name about a decade later): confirmed.
Pietra Marina and Rovittello of 1990 shown at Vinitaly in 1993 (the house's 2020 profile): confirmed as the house's.
Monte Serra at Viagrande in 1998 and Serra della Contessa from the 1998 vintage (the house's timeline and profile): confirmed.
Giuseppe Benanti died on 1 February 2023 aged 78 (Wine Spectator, its memorial list of 2023), born in July 1945 by the house's profile: confirmed, 1945 to 2023 kept.
The twin sons took charge in 2012 (the house's pages, Wine Spectator): confirmed; they are Antonio and Salvino in both, not Salvatore.

Pietra Marina: Contrada Rinazzo at Milo, about 800 metres, the east slope open to light, sea and wind; picked by hand after the middle of October, pressed softly, about twelve days in steel with the house's own native yeast, about thirty months on the fine lees with frequent bâtonnage, twelve months in bottle (the house's sheet and 2023 profile): confirmed.

The Etna rules: DOC by presidential decree of 11 August 1968, the first of Sicily; Etna Bianco at least 60 per cent Carricante; Etna Bianco Superiore at least 80 per cent from the delimited zone in the commune of Milo (AIS copy, Wikipedia): confirmed.
The house rules: the sons and the oenologist unnamed; British; no dash: sound.

changed.was: Older lists spell the wine Pietramarina in one word; the house prints Pietra Marina, and it is the white, not one of the reds.
changed.now: Many lists spell the wine Pietramarina; the house prints Pietra Marina, and it is not the house's Contrada Rinazzo, a separate Etna Bianco Superiore from the same contrada of Milo.
changed.why: Wine Spectator spelt it Pietramarina in 2023, so the spelling is not only an old one; and the house makes a separate Contrada Rinazzo Etna Bianco Superiore, the nearer confusion now that the record names the contrada.

tested: Founded 1978: the perpetuo begun at Samperi in 1978, the launch of Vecchio Samperi in 1980 as the house's first wine (the house's Quarantennale, Vecchio Samperi and Italian pages): confirmed.

Grillo alone, planted between 1970 and 1996 in Contrada Samperi on mostly limestone, level land of sandy loam, picked in the last week of September, fermented with wild yeasts in oak and chestnut barrels at room temperature, the casks never emptied (the house's English and Italian Vecchio Samperi pages and its brochure): confirmed.
Not fortified, so not Marsala under the rules (the house's pages): confirmed; the Quarantennale reached almost 18 per cent naturally by the house's page.
The founder: born in Marsala on 4 February 1945, died 2011 (the house's founder page); died on 18 March 2011 aged 66 (WineNews, an English wine site's obituary): confirmed, now named with his dates.

Samperi: the family's baglio twelve kilometres from Marsala, where vineyards and cellars have kept the memory for over two centuries (the house's founder page): changed, since the page does not say the family has held it for two centuries.
Bukkuram, the first passito bottled on Pantelleria in 1984 (the house's founder and Bukkuram pages): confirmed.

The charge of 1995 and the acquittal five years later: the Marsala prosecutors' charge of adulteration in 1995 and the acquittal after five years, il fatto non sussiste (Balarm), the winery shut from 1995 to 2000 (Barberry), the founder's own word that he was acquitted (Cronache di Gusto), the winery unjustly shut for a few years (Louis Dressner Selections): confirmed.
The racing career: car racing among the threads of his life on the house's founder page: confirmed in outline, what he raced not found.

The Marsala tiers of the trap: the Codex's own Marsala records (Fine, Superiore, Superiore Riserva, Vergine also labelled Soleras, Vergine Stravecchio or Riserva): confirmed; the question's option of a Soleras rank changed.
The house rules: the children unnamed; British; no dash: sound.

tested: Founded 1980 by three friends whose surnames give the initials, the first harvest of 5 October 1980 with 1,470 bottles, the family cellar and vineyard passed to them by one founder's father (the house's company page): confirmed; the training of those vines not given, so bush vines is cut.
1985: one founder chose medicine and sold his share to his sister (the house's pages): confirmed.
September 2000: the first amphorae from Spain, and Pithos born (the house's pages): confirmed.

The rules: DOC by decree of 29 May 1973, published 28 August 1973, amended in 1991; DOCG by ministerial decree of 13 September 2005, the only one in Sicily; Nero d'Avola 50 to 70 per cent, Frappato 30 to 50, no other grape; the Classico held back until 31 March of the second year after the harvest, plain Cerasuolo until 1 June of the next (AIS copy, a copy of the disciplinare, Quattrocalici, Wikipedia, Wein.plus): confirmed; the house's own page gives 1974 for the DOC.
The house's claim that its 2005 wine was the first to carry the DOCG (the house's page on Cerasuolo and Pithos): confirmed as the house's claim.
The site: 230 metres, limestone 30 to 60 centimetres down under red clay, red soils of sand of Pliocene origin (the house's home page and its 2012 page): confirmed.

The making of the Classico: spontaneous fermentation on the skins in concrete tanks with native yeasts (Flatiron Wines, Callmewine); eighteen months in Slavonian oak botti, or a year in botti and a year in concrete; 24 months in foudres with a year in concrete belongs to the Classico della Bastonaca: changed, old casks not found.
The blend of the house's Classico, about 60 per cent Nero d'Avola and 40 Frappato in several listings: confirmed.
The library's biodynamic farming: the house's own archive carries a page on biodynamics and amphora, so the library is not contradicted; the record says nothing of the farming.
The house rules: the founders and the sister unnamed; British; no dash: sound.
